newsitem.title: LEBANON: BLC Q1 results "very good" - financiers.
newsitem.headline: BLC Q1 results "very good" - financiers.

text.p: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce first quarter results announced on Monday are on target and promise a quick appreciation of the bank's stock, financiers said on Tuesday.
BLC reported consolidated pre-tax profits of 8.04 billion Lebanese pounds ($5.2 million), including 2.80 billion ($1.81 million) realised on the sale of real estate assets.
"The results are very good. They are in line with forecasts and expectations," said Georges Abou Jaoude, director of Lebanese operations at Financial Funds Advisors, a Beirut Finance house.
Nicholas Sawan, deputy manager and head of trading at Lebanon Invest, said: "Bearing in mind that the first quarter is usually the worst for profits, BLC results are quite good."

The land sale was on track in light of the bank's plan to sell $8 million worth of land in 1997 -- part of a three-year plan to realise $25 million extraordinary profits in real estate sales, he said.
Abou Jaoude calculated BLC's current price/earnings ratio at 10 on the basis of the results.
P.E. ratios for Banque Audi and Bank of Beirut were 11.75 and around 14 respectively. The shares traded at $20 and $3.5625 on Tuesday.
"The share is undervalued compared to other shares on the market. It is trading at a discount," Abou Jaoude said.
BLC shares have risen 48.8 percent since they began trading on the Beirut Stock Exchange last December. The share traded at $16.75 on Tuesday, falling for the second straight day on profit-taking.

"As soon as the market gets aware of the fact that the share is undervalued, you will start seeing demand on BLC and the stock will start heading towards higher targets. I see it up to $20 in the short run," Sawan said.
Audi reported $5.2 million in net profits for the first quarter of 1997 while BOB reported a 29.6 percent increase in profits during the same period.
